name: Keyboard (No Exception)
explanation: This is the stricter, no-exceptions version of SC 2.1.1 Keyboard. The Level A version allows one narrow exception, for functions that depend on the path of a movement, like freehand drawing. This AAA criterion removes that exception entirely. Every single piece of functionality must be operable from a keyboard, with no exception at all. In practice, this means path-dependent interactions need a fully keyboard-operable alternative. If no such alternative is possible, the feature can't be offered at all under this stricter bar.
whoItAffects: This affects the same people as SC 2.1.1: keyboard-only users, switch-device users, and voice-control users whose software emulates keyboard input. Meeting this AAA criterion closes a small gap the Level A exception leaves open. That gap covers rare cases like freehand signature capture or gesture-based drawing tools. Without a keyboard alternative, those tools stay unusable even on a site that's otherwise fully compliant.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- A freehand signature pad with no keyboard-operable alternative -->
<canvas id="signature-pad" aria-label="Draw your signature"></canvas>
<!-- Mouse/touch drawing only; there is no other way to provide a signature -->
codeExample.good:
<!-- The signature pad remains for mouse/touch users, but a fully
     keyboard-operable alternative satisfies the input requirement -->
<canvas id="signature-pad" aria-label="Draw your signature"></canvas>
<button type="button" id="type-signature">Type your name instead</button>
<!-- Typing a name is a keyboard-operable equivalent path to the same
     underlying requirement: providing a signature -->

howToTest: Find any feature on the page that depends on the path of a pointer movement, not just its start and end point. Freehand drawing, gesture-based games, and signature capture are common examples. For each one, check whether a keyboard-only user has some way to do the same underlying task, even if the interaction looks different. Typing a name instead of drawing a signature is one example. If no keyboard path exists at all for that functionality, it fails this criterion.

check.question: A site offers a freehand drawing tool for annotating photos, usable only with a mouse or touchscreen, with no keyboard-operable alternative for adding annotations. Does this meet SC 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception)?
choices: Yes, because freehand drawing is exempted the same way it is under SC 2.1.1
No, because this AAA criterion has no path-dependent exception, so an equivalent keyboard-operable way to annotate is required
Yes, because AAA criteria are optional and never required for conformance
It depends on whether the tool also supports touch input
